question: What is reported about peer instruction clicker questions and conceptual exam performance?
required_claim: Peer discussion after clicker questions is linked to conceptual gains; one source notes weaker effects without trained facilitators.

passages.text: The swimming pool closed for tile repairs over the long weekend.
A lost-and-found notice listed three umbrellas and a calculator.
Bus route 12 added an evening stop near the graduate housing block.
Study PI-1 found that classes using peer discussion after clicker questions showed higher conceptual exam scores than lecture-only controls.
A cafeteria recipe change reduced sodium in the soup of the day.
Study PI-2 reported weaker or null conceptual gains when peer instruction was used without facilitator training and with poorly designed questions.
The alumni office mailed reunion invitations to the class of 2014.
